trust_decision.summary: Which caller-supplied path segments may be used as property keys when walking/creating nested objects; at the pinned commit only the FIRST segment is compared against '__proto__' in set() and transform(), so later segments and 'constructor'/'prototype' are trusted.

landing_point.why: The summary names set() first; its existing '__proto__' first-segment guard is the obvious line to widen.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API dottie.set(object, path, value, options); also reached via dottie['default'](object, path, value)
public API dottie.transform(object, options); also reached via the callable dottie(object) with one argument
fix_sites.module_kind: core library function, separate path-walking implementation in the same file

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: dottie.js:139-168 (transform has its own nested-write loop, separate from set at dottie.js:81-105); wrappers dottie.js:112-116 (default) and dottie.js:19-26 (callable) reach the two sites but need no change

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: the advisory summary names both set() and transform(), so a solver has little room to argue transform is out of scope; the wrappers are fixed automatically by fixing set/transform.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Normal dotted paths and look-alike key names (e.g. 'user.proto.value') must keep working in set and transform; transform must keep copying non-delimited keys and honour a custom delimiter; set must keep its `force` overwrite behaviour.

O6_input_shapes: transform(): keys split on a custom options.delimiter (dottie.js:127, dottie.js:143)
transform(): array of objects, mapped recursively (dottie.js:120-124)
dangerous segment at any position, not only the first (fix.diff:18, fix.diff:30)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: dottie['default'] rewritten with its own nested walker (to avoid the double traversal of get()+set()) instead of delegating to set()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: default() already walks the path once via get(); a maintainer optimising it would plausibly inline the write loop and copy set()'s original first-segment-only guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: set() reusing the get() memoized split-path cache, so pieces come from the cache rather than the checked split
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: get() already memoizes path splits for speed; extending that to set() is a natural perf change and moves the pieces across a cache boundary.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an unflatten()/merge-style helper next to flatten() that rebuilds nested objects from delimited keys with its own loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: flatten() has no inverse besides transform(); a symmetric helper (or deep-merge of defaults) in this file is a plausible addition and would be a third write implementation.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via unchecked path segments in nested-property setters

O10_build.project_tests: test/set.test.js:69-74 and test/transform.test.js:149-158 cover only the first-segment '__proto__' case; run with `npm test` (mocha over test/)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change set()'s `pieces[0] === '__proto__'` to check every segment for '__proto__' only, leaving transform() and the 'constructor'/'prototype' segments unchecked.

out_of_scope_notes: The published guard compares segments with strict equality (fix.diff:18), so non-string elements of an array path that coerce to a dangerous key are not matched; this is a residual weakness of the fix itself and was not pursued.
transform() uses `break` on a dangerous key (dottie.js:145, kept by fix.diff:30), which silently drops all later keys instead of skipping one; behavioural quirk, not pursued.

transform() copies a non-delimited '__proto__' key straight onto the result object (dottie.js:165-166); this changes only that result object's own prototype, not the global one, so it is outside this advisory's sink.
